title: Object name is a reserved word
rationale: A reserved word used as an identifier must be double-quoted everywhere forever. Any tool, ORM or ad-hoc query that omits the quotes fails at runtime rather than at migration time.
sql: SELECT owner, object_name, object_type, 'Object name "' || object_name || '" is a reserved word' AS detail FROM v_user_objects WHERE UPPER(object_name) IN ('ORDER','GROUP','SELECT','TABLE','INDEX','SESSION','SIZE','COMMENT','LEVEL','DATE','NUMBER','ROW','ROWS','START','CHECK','CLUSTER','ACCESS','AUDIT','MODE','RESOURCE','SHARE','UID','USER','VALUES','VIEW','PUBLIC','RAW','LONG','FILE','TYPE','ONLINE','OFFLINE','MINUS','DEFAULT','EXCLUSIVE','IDENTIFIED','IMMEDIATE','INCREMENT','INITIAL','LOCK','MAXEXTENTS','NOAUDIT','NOCOMPRESS','NOWAIT','OPTION','PCTFREE','PRIOR','SUCCESSFUL','SYNONYM','SYSDATE','THEN','TRIGGER','VALIDATE','WHENEVER')

title: Column name is a reserved word
rationale: Same failure mode as a reserved-word table name, but harder to spot because it only surfaces when that specific column is referenced unquoted.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name || '.' || column_name AS object_name, 'COLUMN' AS object_type, 'Column "' || column_name || '" is a reserved word' AS detail FROM v_user_columns WHERE UPPER(column_name) IN ('ORDER','GROUP','SELECT','TABLE','INDEX','SESSION','SIZE','COMMENT','LEVEL','DATE','NUMBER','ROW','ROWS','START','CHECK','ACCESS','AUDIT','MODE','RESOURCE','SHARE','UID','USER','VALUES','VIEW','RAW','LONG','FILE','TYPE','ONLINE','OFFLINE','MINUS','DEFAULT','PRIOR','THEN','VALIDATE')

title: Directory object requires S3 integration on RDS
rationale: RDS for Oracle gives no operating-system filesystem access. A DIRECTORY pointing at a local path has no equivalent; file exchange must go through S3_INTEGRATION.
sql: SELECT owner, directory_name AS object_name, 'DIRECTORY' AS object_type, 'Directory points at ' || directory_path || '; no OS filesystem on RDS' AS detail FROM directories WHERE directory_name NOT LIKE 'ORACLE_%' AND directory_name NOT LIKE 'OPATCH%' AND directory_name NOT LIKE 'DATA_PUMP%' AND directory_name NOT LIKE 'JAVA$%' AND directory_name NOT LIKE 'DBMS_OPTIM%'

title: External table cannot be migrated as-is
rationale: An external table reads a file from the database server's filesystem. RDS has none, so the table will exist but return nothing. The data source must move to S3 or the table must be replaced.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name AS object_name, 'EXTERNAL TABLE' AS object_type, 'Reads from directory ' || COALESCE(default_directory_name,'?') || '; unsupported on RDS without S3 integration' AS detail FROM external_tables

title: Database link requires re-creation and network path
rationale: Links are not carried by Data Pump in usable form. The target needs the link recreated and a network route plus credentials to the remote database.
sql: SELECT owner, db_link AS object_name, 'DATABASE LINK' AS object_type, 'Link to ' || COALESCE(SUBSTR(host,1,60),'?') || ' must be recreated with a valid network path' AS detail FROM db_links WHERE owner <> 'PUBLIC'

title: Scheduler job needs review after cutover
rationale: Jobs migrate but resume on the target on their existing schedule. An unreviewed job can run against production the moment the instance opens.
sql: SELECT owner, job_name AS object_name, 'JOB' AS object_type, 'Job is ' || COALESCE(enabled,'?') || '; confirm schedule and privileges on target' AS detail FROM scheduler_jobs

title: Advanced Queuing objects present
rationale: AQ queues carry internal state and subscribers that Data Pump does not reliably reproduce. Queues normally need recreating and draining before cutover.
sql: SELECT owner, name AS object_name, 'QUEUE' AS object_type, 'Queue on table ' || COALESCE(queue_table,'?') || ' needs recreation and drain before cutover' AS detail FROM queues

title: Oracle Text index requires option group configuration
rationale: A CONTEXT index depends on Oracle Text being present in the RDS option group. Without it the index cannot be created and dependent queries fail.
sql: SELECT owner, index_name AS object_name, 'INDEX' AS object_type, 'Domain index of type ' || COALESCE(index_type,'?') || ' requires Oracle Text in the option group' AS detail FROM indexes WHERE index_type LIKE 'DOMAIN%'

title: Registered XML schema must be re-registered on target
rationale: XMLType columns bound to a registered schema fail to load if the schema is not registered on the target first, and Data Pump ordering does not guarantee that.
sql: SELECT owner, schema_url AS object_name, 'XML SCHEMA' AS object_type, 'XML schema must be registered on the target before dependent tables load' AS detail FROM xml_schemas

title: User-defined type is not supported by DMS
rationale: AWS DMS does not replicate user-defined object types. Tables with object columns need Data Pump or a redesign, which changes the movement strategy for those tables.
sql: SELECT owner, type_name AS object_name, 'TYPE' AS object_type, 'Object type (' || COALESCE(typecode,'?') || ') is not replicated by DMS' AS detail FROM types WHERE predefined = 'NO'

title: Materialized view needs refresh strategy on target
rationale: An MV and its log must be rebuilt and re-primed on the target. Migrating the container table alone leaves a view that never refreshes.
sql: SELECT owner, mview_name AS object_name, 'MATERIALIZED VIEW' AS object_type, 'Refresh mode ' || COALESCE(refresh_mode,'?') || '/' || COALESCE(refresh_method,'?') || ' must be rebuilt on target' AS detail FROM materialized_views

title: LOB column affects DMS load configuration
rationale: DMS truncates LOBs silently in limited-LOB mode and runs far slower in full-LOB mode. The choice must be deliberate and sized, not defaulted.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name || '.' || column_name AS object_name, 'LOB' AS object_type, 'LOB column; DMS LOB mode and max size must be set explicitly' AS detail FROM lobs

title: Partitioned table requires Enterprise Edition
rationale: Partitioning is not available on RDS SE2 at any price. A partitioned source either forces EE BYOL or the partitions must be collapsed, which changes performance characteristics.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name AS object_name, 'TABLE' AS object_type, partitioning_type || ' partitioned with ' || CAST(partition_count AS TEXT) || ' partitions; requires EE on RDS' AS detail FROM partitioned_tables

title: Synonym may resolve to an object that does not migrate
rationale: A synonym pointing across a database link or at a schema outside the migration scope becomes a broken reference on the target.
sql: SELECT owner, synonym_name AS object_name, 'SYNONYM' AS object_type, 'Synonym resolves to ' || COALESCE(table_owner,'?') || '.' || COALESCE(table_name,'?') || COALESCE('@' || db_link,'') AS detail FROM synonyms WHERE db_link IS NOT NULL OR table_owner NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT owner FROM v_user_tables)

title: Source character set must match the target
rationale: Creating the RDS instance with a different character set silently corrupts non-ASCII data on load. The target must be created with this value; it cannot be changed afterwards.
sql: SELECT NULL AS owner, parameter AS object_name, 'NLS' AS object_type, 'Source is ' || value || '; RDS instance must be created with this character set' AS detail FROM nls_parameters WHERE parameter = 'NLS_CHARACTERSET'

title: Table has no primary key
rationale: DMS change data capture cannot reliably apply updates or deletes to a table with no primary key or unique index. Rows can be duplicated or missed during CDC with no error raised.
sql: SELECT t.owner, t.table_name AS object_name, 'TABLE' AS object_type, 'No primary key; DMS CDC cannot reliably replicate updates or deletes' AS detail FROM v_user_tables t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM constraints c WHERE c.owner = t.owner AND c.table_name = t.table_name AND c.constraint_type = 'P')

title: Near-unique column contains duplicate values
rationale: A column the optimizer treats as almost unique but which carries duplicates is a natural key with no enforcement. Adding a unique constraint on the target will fail until the duplicates are resolved.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name || '.' || column_name AS object_name, 'COLUMN' AS object_type, CAST(duplicate_count AS TEXT) || ' duplicate values in a column with no unique constraint' || CASE WHEN sampled = 'Y' THEN ' (found in a ' || CAST(sample_pct AS TEXT) || '% sample -- the true count is higher)' ELSE '' END AS detail FROM column_profile WHERE duplicate_count > 0

title: Text column contains non-ASCII characters
rationale: Characters outside ASCII are usually legitimate, but a cp1252 artifact such as CHR(146) becomes a replacement character or a load failure when the target character set differs.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name || '.' || column_name AS object_name, 'COLUMN' AS object_type, CAST(non_ascii_count AS TEXT) || ' rows contain characters outside ASCII; verify against target character set' || CASE WHEN sampled = 'Y' THEN ' (found in a ' || CAST(sample_pct AS TEXT) || '% sample -- the true count is higher)' ELSE '' END AS detail FROM column_profile WHERE non_ascii_count > 0

title: Constraint is enabled but not validated
rationale: ENABLE NOVALIDATE means existing rows were never checked. Data that violates the constraint is already present and will fail a validated rebuild on the target.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name || '.' || constraint_name AS object_name, 'CONSTRAINT' AS object_type, 'Constraint type ' || constraint_type || ' is ENABLE NOVALIDATE; pre-existing rows may violate it' AS detail FROM constraints WHERE validated = 'NOT VALIDATED' AND status = 'ENABLED'

title: Constraint is disabled
rationale: A disabled constraint enforces nothing, so the data behind it is unverified. Re-enabling it on the target may fail.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name || '.' || constraint_name AS object_name, 'CONSTRAINT' AS object_type, 'Constraint is DISABLED and enforcing nothing' AS detail FROM constraints WHERE status = 'DISABLED'

title: NUMBER column has no precision or scale
rationale: An unconstrained NUMBER accepts up to 38 digits with arbitrary scale. Mapping it to a fixed-width type on any target risks silent truncation or overflow.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name || '.' || column_name AS object_name, 'COLUMN' AS object_type, 'NUMBER with no precision or scale; mapping risk to a fixed-width target type' AS detail FROM v_user_columns WHERE data_type = 'NUMBER' AND data_precision IS NULL AND data_scale IS NULL

title: Optimizer statistics are stale or missing
rationale: Sizing and cardinality decisions read these statistics. Stale numbers produce a wrong target size and hide data-quality problems that only cardinality would reveal.
sql: SELECT t.owner, t.table_name AS object_name, 'TABLE' AS object_type, CASE WHEN t.last_analyzed IS NULL THEN 'Never analyzed' ELSE 'Last analyzed ' || t.last_analyzed END || '; sizing and cardinality decisions read these statistics' AS detail FROM v_user_tables t WHERE t.last_analyzed IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM table_profile p WHERE p.owner = t.owner AND p.table_name = t.table_name AND p.actual_rows IS NOT NULL AND t.num_rows IS NOT NULL AND ABS(p.actual_rows - t.num_rows) > 0)

title: Column contains only NULLs
rationale: An entirely NULL column is either dead weight to drop before migration or evidence that a load never populated it. Either way it should be a decision, not an accident.
sql: SELECT c.owner, c.table_name || '.' || c.column_name AS object_name, 'COLUMN' AS object_type, 'Every row is NULL across ' || CAST(c.num_nulls AS TEXT) || ' rows' AS detail FROM v_user_columns c WHERE c.num_nulls > 0 AND c.num_distinct = 0

title: Character column uses byte length semantics
rationale: BYTE semantics on a multibyte character set truncates at fewer characters than the declared length suggests. Moving to AL32UTF8 can overflow columns that fit today.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name || '.' || column_name AS object_name, 'COLUMN' AS object_type, 'VARCHAR2 declared with BYTE semantics; may overflow on a multibyte target character set' AS detail FROM v_user_columns WHERE char_used = 'B' AND data_type IN ('VARCHAR2','CHAR')

title: Table could not be profiled for data quality
rationale: A table that was not profiled has no data-quality evidence behind it. The absence of findings is not the same as the absence of problems, and the report must not imply otherwise.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name AS object_name, 'TABLE' AS object_type, 'Not profiled: ' || skip_reason AS detail FROM table_profile WHERE profiled = 'N' AND skip_reason NOT IN ('oracle_internal_object')

title: Table was profiled by sample, not in full
rationale: Sampling makes a large table affordable to profile, but it changes what a clean result means. Finding a duplicate in a sample proves duplicates exist; finding none does not prove they are absent. Data-quality findings on these tables are a lower bound.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name AS object_name, 'TABLE' AS object_type, 'Profiled from a ' || CAST(sample_pct AS TEXT) || '% sample of an estimated ' || CAST(estimated_rows AS TEXT) || ' rows; a clean result here is not proof of absence' AS detail FROM table_profile WHERE sampled = 'Y'

title: Foreign key has no supporting index
rationale: An unindexed foreign key forces a full scan of the child table on parent delete or update, and in Oracle takes a share lock on the child table while it does so. It is the classic cause of migration-day lock contention.
sql: SELECT c.owner, c.table_name || '.' || cc.column_name AS object_name, 'FOREIGN KEY' AS object_type, 'FK column has no index with it in the leading position; delete and update on the parent will scan and lock' AS detail FROM constraints c JOIN constraint_columns cc ON cc.owner = c.owner AND cc.constraint_name = c.constraint_name WHERE c.constraint_type = 'R' AND cc.position = 1 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM index_columns ic WHERE ic.table_owner = c.owner AND ic.table_name = c.table_name AND ic.column_name = cc.column_name AND ic.column_position = 1)

title: Table has no indexes at all
rationale: Every access is a full scan. Tolerable while the table is small, but it is also a signal that access patterns were never considered.
sql: SELECT t.owner, t.table_name AS object_name, 'TABLE' AS object_type, 'No indexes; every access is a full table scan' AS detail FROM v_user_tables t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM indexes i WHERE i.table_owner = t.owner AND i.table_name = t.table_name)

title: Table carries an unusually high number of indexes
rationale: Every index is re-applied after the data load and maintained on every DML. A large index count materially extends the migration window and slows writes afterwards.
sql: SELECT i.table_owner AS owner, i.table_name AS object_name, 'TABLE' AS object_type, CAST(COUNT(*) AS TEXT) || ' indexes on one table; each is rebuilt after load and maintained on every write' AS detail FROM indexes i WHERE i.table_name IN (SELECT table_name FROM v_user_tables) GROUP BY i.table_owner, i.table_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 6

title: Index is unusable or invisible
rationale: An unusable index is not maintained and not used; an invisible one is maintained but ignored by the optimizer. Both migrate as dead weight unless the state is deliberate.
sql: SELECT owner, index_name AS object_name, 'INDEX' AS object_type, 'Index status ' || COALESCE(status,'?') || ', visibility ' || COALESCE(visibility,'?') AS detail FROM indexes WHERE status = 'UNUSABLE' OR visibility = 'INVISIBLE'

title: Table shows significant row chaining
rationale: Chained rows span blocks, so each read costs extra I/O. A migration is the natural point to fix it, because the rebuild happens anyway.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name AS object_name, 'TABLE' AS object_type, CAST(chain_cnt AS TEXT) || ' chained rows; each spans blocks and costs extra I/O per read' AS detail FROM v_user_tables WHERE chain_cnt > 0

title: Large table is not partitioned
rationale: A large unpartitioned table loads as a single DMS task with no parallelism and cannot be archived by partition afterwards. Worth a deliberate decision before the move.
sql: SELECT s.owner, s.segment_name AS object_name, 'TABLE' AS object_type, 'Segment is ' || CAST(ROUND(SUM(s.bytes)/1048576.0) AS TEXT) || ' MB and not partitioned; loads as a single serial task' AS detail FROM segments s WHERE s.segment_type = 'TABLE' AND s.segment_name IN (SELECT table_name FROM v_user_tables) AND s.segment_name NOT IN (SELECT table_name FROM partitioned_tables) GROUP BY s.owner, s.segment_name HAVING SUM(s.bytes) > 268435456

title: Index has a poor clustering factor
rationale: A clustering factor approaching the row count means range scans read almost one block per row, so the optimizer will usually prefer a full scan and the index earns little.
sql: SELECT i.owner, i.index_name AS object_name, 'INDEX' AS object_type, 'Clustering factor ' || CAST(i.clustering_factor AS TEXT) || ' against ' || CAST(i.num_rows AS TEXT) || ' rows; range scans approach one block per row' AS detail FROM indexes i WHERE i.num_rows > 10000 AND i.clustering_factor > (i.num_rows * 0.9)

title: Redundant index on the same leading column
rationale: Two indexes sharing a leading column often means one is never chosen. Both are still rebuilt after the load and maintained on every write.
sql: SELECT a.index_owner AS owner, a.table_name || ' (' || a.column_name || ')' AS object_name, 'INDEX' AS object_type, 'Indexes ' || a.index_name || ' and ' || b.index_name || ' share leading column ' || a.column_name AS detail FROM index_columns a JOIN index_columns b ON a.table_name = b.table_name AND a.column_name = b.column_name AND a.column_position = 1 AND b.column_position = 1 AND a.index_name < b.index_name WHERE a.table_name IN (SELECT table_name FROM v_user_tables)

title: Invalid object will not compile
rationale: An object that does not compile on the source will not compile on the target either. Migrating it moves a known-broken object into production and masks the failure among expected post-load invalidations.
sql: SELECT owner, object_name, object_type, 'Object status is ' || status || '; resolve before migration' AS detail FROM invalid_objects

title: Privilege granted to PUBLIC
rationale: A grant to PUBLIC is a grant to every current and future database user. It migrates silently and widens access on the target by default.
sql: SELECT grantee AS owner, owner || '.' || table_name AS object_name, 'GRANT' AS object_type, privilege || ' granted to PUBLIC' AS detail FROM table_privileges WHERE grantee = 'PUBLIC'

title: Powerful ANY system privilege granted
rationale: ANY privileges cross schema boundaries entirely. They are rarely needed by an application account and should not be carried to the target unexamined.
sql: SELECT grantee AS owner, privilege AS object_name, 'SYSTEM PRIVILEGE' AS object_type, 'Account holds ' || privilege || ', which crosses schema boundaries' AS detail FROM system_privileges WHERE privilege LIKE '%ANY%'

title: Application account holds DBA or elevated role
rationale: An application schema with DBA can do anything on the target, including bypass the controls this migration is meant to preserve.
sql: SELECT grantee AS owner, granted_role AS object_name, 'ROLE' AS object_type, 'Account holds role ' || granted_role AS detail FROM role_privileges WHERE granted_role IN ('DBA','IMP_FULL_DATABASE','EXP_FULL_DATABASE','DATAPUMP_IMP_FULL_DATABASE','SELECT_ANY_DICTIONARY')

title: Account has unlimited tablespace
rationale: UNLIMITED TABLESPACE removes any storage ceiling on the account. On RDS, where storage is billed and autoscaled, that becomes a cost exposure as well as an operational one.
sql: SELECT grantee AS owner, privilege AS object_name, 'SYSTEM PRIVILEGE' AS object_type, 'Account can consume storage without limit' AS detail FROM system_privileges WHERE privilege = 'UNLIMITED TABLESPACE'

title: Password never expires
rationale: A profile with unlimited password life means credentials migrated to the target stay valid indefinitely, including any that were shared during the migration itself.
sql: SELECT NULL AS owner, profile AS object_name, 'PROFILE' AS object_type, 'PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME is ' || "limit" || '; credentials never expire' AS detail FROM profiles WHERE resource_name = 'PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME' AND "limit" = 'UNLIMITED'

title: Column name suggests sensitive data without encryption
rationale: Columns holding national identifiers or similar are candidates for TDE or application-level encryption. TDE on RDS requires Enterprise Edition, so this also bears on the edition decision.
sql: SELECT owner, table_name || '.' || column_name AS object_name, 'COLUMN' AS object_type, 'Column name suggests sensitive data; no encryption detected on source' AS detail FROM v_user_columns WHERE (UPPER(column_name) LIKE '%NATIONAL_ID%' OR UPPER(column_name) LIKE '%SSN%' OR UPPER(column_name) LIKE '%PASSPORT%' OR UPPER(column_name) LIKE '%TAX_ID%' OR UPPER(column_name) LIKE '%CARD_NUMBER%' OR UPPER(column_name) LIKE '%PASSWORD%')

title: Account is locked or expired
rationale: A locked or expired account still migrates, complete with its grants. It is either dead weight to remove or an access path someone forgot about.
sql: SELECT NULL AS owner, username AS object_name, 'USER' AS object_type, 'Account status is ' || account_status AS detail FROM users WHERE oracle_maintained = 'N' AND account_status <> 'OPEN'

title: Database is not in ARCHIVELOG mode
rationale: DMS change data capture reads redo. Without ARCHIVELOG there is no CDC, which means no near-zero-downtime cutover -- only a full outage load.
sql: SELECT NULL AS owner, name AS object_name, 'DATABASE' AS object_type, 'Log mode is ' || log_mode || '; DMS CDC requires ARCHIVELOG' AS detail FROM database WHERE log_mode <> 'ARCHIVELOG'

title: Supplemental logging is not enabled
rationale: Without minimum supplemental logging, redo records omit the column data DMS needs to build an UPDATE on the target. CDC starts and then silently applies incomplete changes.
sql: SELECT NULL AS owner, name AS object_name, 'DATABASE' AS object_type, 'Minimum supplemental logging is ' || COALESCE(supplemental_log_data_min,'?') || '; DMS CDC needs it enabled' AS detail FROM database WHERE supplemental_log_data_min IS NULL OR supplemental_log_data_min NOT IN ('YES','IMPLICIT')

title: Edition-forcing feature is in use
rationale: This feature is unavailable on RDS SE2 at any price. Its detected use is what forces Enterprise Edition BYOL, and it is the single largest driver of the licensing case.
sql: SELECT NULL AS owner, name AS object_name, 'FEATURE' AS object_type, 'Detected ' || CAST(detected_usages AS TEXT) || ' usages, currently_used=' || COALESCE(currently_used,'?') || '; not available on RDS SE2' AS detail FROM feature_usage WHERE edition_forcing = 'Y' AND detected_usages > 0

title: PL/SQL object has stored compilation errors
rationale: Stored errors mean the object is broken now, not merely stale. It needs fixing before migration or it becomes a post-cutover incident.
sql: SELECT owner, name || ' (' || type || ')' AS object_name, 'PLSQL' AS object_type, 'Line ' || CAST(line AS TEXT) || ': ' || SUBSTR(text, 1, 120) AS detail FROM plsql_errors

title: Scheduler job has a failure history
rationale: A job already failing on the source will keep failing on the target, and the migration will be blamed for it.
sql: SELECT owner, job_name AS object_name, 'JOB' AS object_type, CAST(failure_count AS TEXT) || ' failures against ' || CAST(run_count AS TEXT) || ' runs' AS detail FROM scheduler_jobs WHERE failure_count > 0

title: Utilization data is unavailable for sizing
rationale: Instance sizing should rest on observed utilization percentiles. This source exposes no usable metric history, so any sizing recommendation rests on capacity and feature use alone -- and the report must say so rather than imply measured headroom.
sql: SELECT NULL AS owner, 'V$SYSMETRIC' AS object_name, 'METRIC' AS object_type, 'No rows in v$sysmetric; utilization percentiles are not available from this source' AS detail FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM system_metrics) WHERE n = 0

title: Object depends on a database link
rationale: A view or synonym reaching through a link fails on the target until the link is recreated and the network path opened. These break after cutover, not during it.
sql: SELECT owner, synonym_name AS object_name, 'SYNONYM' AS object_type, 'Resolves through database link ' || db_link AS detail FROM synonyms WHERE db_link IS NOT NULL

title: Estate size drives the migration window
rationale: Total segment size sets the floor on load time and the target storage allocation. It is the number every migration plan is built on.
sql: SELECT owner, 'TOTAL_SEGMENT_SIZE' AS object_name, 'ESTATE' AS object_type, CAST(ROUND(SUM(bytes)/1073741824.0, 3) AS TEXT) || ' GB across ' || CAST(COUNT(*) AS TEXT) || ' segments' AS detail FROM segments GROUP BY owner HAVING SUM(bytes) > 0

title: Oracle Text index contains no documents
rationale: A CONTEXT index created before its table was populated, or never synced after a load, reports INDEXED and VALID while indexing nothing. Searches against it return no rows and raise no error, so the fault survives migration unnoticed and is blamed on the migration. Rebuilding it on the target is cheap; discovering it after cutover is not.
sql: SELECT ti.owner, ti.index_name AS object_name, 'INDEX' AS object_type, 'Text index holds ' || ti.docid_count || ' document(s) but ' || ti.table_name || ' has ' || t.num_rows || ' row(s); searches return nothing until it is rebuilt or synced' AS detail FROM text_indexes ti JOIN tables t ON t.owner = ti.table_owner AND t.table_name = ti.table_name WHERE COALESCE(ti.docid_count, 0) = 0 AND COALESCE(t.num_rows, 0) > 0
